title: Principles of Information Security
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This CIA component ensures only authorized users can read the data

categoryLegend: CIA & Foundations: the CIA triad, vulnerabilities, risk, attack surface. Threat Landscape: social engineering, malware families, threat actors, APTs. Network Defense: firewalls, IDS/IPS, VPNs, encryption. OS & Hardening: least privilege, system file integrity, attack-surface reduction. Security Mindset: MFA, access-control models, incident response, defense in depth.

clues.clue: This component of the CIA triad ensures that data is only accessible to authorized users.
A threat actor modifies patient records in a hospital database without authorization. This CIA triad component is primarily violated.
The total set of all entry points where an attacker could try to enter, extract data from, or disrupt a system. Reducing it is a core security goal.
A CDC database is taken down by a DDoS attack during an outbreak response. This is the CIA triad component being violated.
A nation-state actor deploys malware that lies dormant for six months before activating, prioritizing stealth and long-term persistence over speed.
clues.response: What is an APT (Advanced Persistent Threat)?

clues.clue: A social engineer fabricates a scenario, impersonates a doctor, and convinces the help desk to reset a password. This social-engineering technique.
Malware that encrypts the victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key.
This kind of malware self-replicates across a network without needing to attach to a host file, often consuming bandwidth and crashing systems.
The category of threat actor that is most often motivated by financial gain and typically operates as part of an organized criminal syndicate.
An attacker conducts targeted email recon and crafts a personalized lure aimed at one specific high-value executive.
clues.response: What is spear phishing (or whaling for C-suite targets)?

clues.clue: A firewall that tracks the state of active connections and allows only packets belonging to established sessions.
A network device that detects suspicious traffic and generates alerts but does NOT actively block the packets.
clues.response: What is an IDS (Intrusion Detection System)?

clues.clue: The 128, 192, or 256-bit symmetric encryption algorithm that is the current US federal standard.
A next-generation firewall extends a traditional packet filter with deep packet inspection, application awareness, and integration of THIS prevention component.
clues.response: What is an IPS (Intrusion Prevention System)?

clues.clue: This VPN protocol pairing wraps an L2TP tunnel inside IPSec to add encryption and authentication, long used for site-to-site and remote-access links.
The security principle that grants users only the minimum permissions needed to perform their job function.
The Windows command that scans for and repairs corrupted protected system files.
The hardening discipline of removing unused services, default accounts, and unnecessary open ports.
clues.response: What is attack surface reduction (or system hardening)?

clues.clue: The boot-time security feature that uses cryptographic signatures to verify each component (firmware, bootloader, kernel) before it loads.
On Linux, this single character at the end of a permission string indicates a sticky bit on a directory.
MFA requires factors from at least two of these three categories: something you know, something you have, and this third one.
clues.response: What is something you are (a biometric)?

clues.clue: The access control model that grants or denies access based on sensitivity labels assigned to data and clearances assigned to users.
The control that prevents any single employee from both approving AND executing the same financial transaction.
The first phase of the NIST incident response lifecycle: the one that happens BEFORE any incident occurs.
The strategy of layering multiple overlapping security controls so the failure of any one does not breach the whole system.
